model recall of the pain self-management literature
synthesis: The recorded search returned no records, so nothing has been retrieved or inspected. Four leads recalled from memory are listed for checking: a review of predictors of non-completion, an undated service report on video groups, a before-after evaluation of orientation calls, and a study of people who left group rehabilitation early. None of them has been retrieved, and no certainty can be stated until records are inspected.

items.title: Attendance and completion in group pain management programmes: a systematic review of predictors
items.authors: Marchetti-Oyelaran S, Hagen-Ruiz T, Kobayashi-Fenn L
items.keyFindings: Across studies of group pain programmes, younger age, employment, longer travel and lower expectations of benefit predicted non-completion; most dropout occurred in the first three sessions.
items.limitations: Recalled lead; mixed programme formats; predictors measured at referral, not during the programme.
items.notes: Recalled as a lead after an empty search; not retrieved and not checked.

items.title: Video-delivered versus in-person group pain programmes: attendance and outcomes in a regional service
items.keyFindings: In a regional service, video groups reached more working-age adults and had similar completion to in-person groups, but participants reported weaker group connection.
items.limitations: Recalled lead with no year, quality rating or grade; service report without a comparison of like groups.
items.notes: Recalled as a lead; year not known.

items.title: Pre-programme orientation calls and dropout from group pain management: a before-after service evaluation
items.keyFindings: A short call before the first session was followed by fewer people leaving after the first two sessions, in one clinic over one year.
items.limitations: Recalled lead; uncontrolled; waiting list and staffing changed at the same time.
items.notes: Recalled as a lead; relevant to one of the three planned adaptations.

items.title: Language, transport and work as barriers to completing group rehabilitation programmes: a study of people who left early
items.keyFindings: People who left group rehabilitation early described inflexible session times, long bus journeys, and sessions in a language they followed only partly.
items.limitations: Recalled lead; cardiac and pulmonary rehabilitation groups rather than pain programmes.
items.notes: Recalled as a lead; supports interviewing people who leave.

summary: Four unchecked leads after an empty search; no certainty proposed.
